12.5 Stroke.summary: Heart failure (HF) and stroke frequently coexist due to shared risk factors; atrial fibrillation (AF) confers additional stroke risk. Stroke incidence is higher early after HF diagnosis or decompensation and decreases over months. Patients with HF and stroke have higher mortality and worse outcomes. Anticoagulation is indicated for HF with concomitant AF when CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥1. Warfarin reduced ischaemic stroke vs aspirin in WARCEF but increased major hemorrhage; meta-analyses show bleeding risk may outweigh benefit for routine anticoagulation in HFrEF with sinus rhythm. COMMANDER-HF: rivaroxaban 2.5 mg b.i.d. did not improve composite outcomes. Consider anticoagulation for visible intraventricular thrombus, high thrombotic risk, peripheral embolism history, PPCM, or LV non-compaction (LVNC).
key_points: HF and stroke often coexist; AF increases stroke risk and mortality.
Incidence of stroke highest in first 30 days after HF diagnosis or episode.
WARCEF: warfarin reduced ischaemic stroke vs aspirin but increased major bleeding.
COMMANDER-HF: low-dose rivaroxaban did not improve composite outcome for all-cause mortality, MI, or stroke.
Anticoagulation recommended for visible intraventricular thrombus or high thrombotic risk conditions (peripheral embolism, PPCM, LVNC).
notable_trials_and_findings: WARCEF trial: warfarin vs aspirin in reduced EF.

13.1 Diabetes.summary: Treatment of HF is similar in patients with and without diabetes. Antidiabetic drugs differ in effects in HF and preference should be given to drugs that are safe and reduce HF-related events. SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) were studied in large CV and CKD trials (EMPA-REG OUTCOME, VERTIS-CV, CANVAS, DECLARE-TIMI 58) showing outcomes in patients with established cardiovascular disease or risk factors and CKD.
key_points: HF treatment similar regardless of diabetes status; choose antidiabetic drugs with proven safety/benefit in HF.
SGLT2 inhibitors have been studied extensively in CV and CKD outcome trials.
notable_drugs_and_trials: SGLT2 inhibitors: canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin
Trials: EMPA-REG OUTCOME, VERTIS-CV, CANVAS, DECLARE-TIMI 58
